q: How do I estimate enteric methane from dairy cattle and buffalo in India?
title: Enteric methane from dairy cattle
short: Multiply the average number of animals by a methane factor per head per year, then by methane's warming potential. With the IPCC 2006 Tier 1 factor for dairy cattle in the Indian subcontinent, 58 kg CH4 a year, times 27 under AR6, each cow comes to about 1.57 tonnes CO2e. Buffalo have their own factor.
audience: Dairy processors and milk-based exporters asked for Scope 3 FLAG data

ol: Count average annual population by type: dairy cows, other cattle, buffalo. For animals present part of the year, use animals x days present / 365.

Apply the per-head factor. IPCC 2006 Volume 4, Chapter 10, Table 10.11 gives 58 kg CH4 a year for dairy cattle and 27 for other cattle in the Indian subcontinent. Take the buffalo factor from the same chapter's Tier 1 tables and note the table number.
Convert to CO2e with a GWP. AR6 gives 27 for methane of non-fossil origin; some programmes still ask for the AR5 value of 28, so use what your buyer or framework specifies and say which.
Divide by milk volume for an intensity per litre.

p: The Tier 1 dairy factor rests on a low milk yield per animal, which the table states beside the factor. Higher yielding cows eat more and emit more methane per head, though less per litre. If your herd yields well above that, or a buyer wants reduction tracking, move to Tier 2, which works from feed intake, digestibility, body weight and milk yield.

The IPCC 2019 Refinement revised enteric factors and groups them by productivity, and India's national inventory reported to the UNFCCC uses country-specific factors. These give different results from the 2006 tables, so name the edition and table you used and keep it the same each year.

sections.h: Where it sits in a dairy company's inventory
ul: Your own herd, if you run farms: Scope 1, as land and livestock (FLAG) emissions.
Milk bought from farmers or cooperatives: Scope 3 Category 1, purchased goods.
Manure management methane and nitrous oxide, feed production and land use change are separate lines, not part of enteric fermentation.
SBTi's FLAG guidance asks companies with significant land-related emissions to set a separate FLAG target; check whether that applies to you.

example.title: Worked example: a milk collection area with 200 dairy cows
lines: Dairy cows: 200 x 58 = 11,600 kg CH4 a year
Intensity = 313,200 / 300,000 = 1.04 kg CO2e per litre, enteric methane only
Buffalo: add head count x the Tier 1 buffalo factor x 27 as a separate line
example.note: Tier 1 factor from IPCC 2006 Table 10.11; the herd size and 1,500 L yield are illustrative. A yield above the Tier 1 assumption means the per-head factor is probably too low, which is a reason to move to Tier 2.
